extracted.intended_audience: The People of the State of New York; voters and citizens interested in constitutional design and the federal judiciary
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive standards and principles for constituting the federal judiciary: how judges are appointed, their tenure and support, safeguards for independence and responsibility, and the proper scope of federal judicial jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of appointing the judges
rubrics_metrics.description: The mode of appointing the judges is the same with that of appointing the officers of the Union in general.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This point encompasses who appoints judges and the appointment process; (the paper notes this was fully discussed in prior numbers and need not be repeated here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure: hold offices DURING GOOD BEHAVIOR
rubrics_metrics.description: All judges appointed by the United States are to hold their offices DURING GOOD BEHAVIOR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Life tenure (during good behavior) is presented as one of the most valuable modern improvements: it secures a steady, upright, and impartial administration of the laws and serves as a citadel of public justice and security by insulating judges from legislative or executive encroachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanency as essential to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanency (continuance in office) contributes critically to the independence of the judiciary and is necessary to defend the courts against influence or overbearing by the other branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the judiciary lacks force and will (having only judgment), permanency helps it resist being overpowered, awed, or influenced by the legislature or executive; temporary commissions or periodic reappointments would undermine needed firmness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fixed provision for judicial support (non-diminishable compensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges 'shall at STATED TIMES receive for their services a compensation which shall not be DIMINISHED during their continuance in office.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A secure, non-diminishable compensation prevents legislative control over judicial subsistence (since 'a power over a man's subsistence amounts to a power over his will'). Compensation may be varied to account for changing circumstances but not reduced as to any sitting judge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precautions for judicial responsibility: impeachment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges are liable to be impeached for malconduct by the House of Representatives and tried by the Senate; if convicted, they may be dismissed and disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impeachment is described as the only provision consistent with necessary judicial independence for removing judges for misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against statutory removal for inability; impracticability of mental-metric removal
rubrics_metrics.description: No special constitutional provision for removing judges on account of inability is provided; attempts to measure mental faculties are impracticable and liable to abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper argues that using age limits or other measures would often be arbitrary or cruel and that insanity, without explicit provision, may be treated as a virtual disqualification. Blanket age cutoffs (e.g., New York's 60-year rule) are criticized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial independence as safeguard of limited Constitution and individual rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete independence of the courts is peculiarly essential in a limited Constitution to preserve specified exceptions to legislative authority and to declare acts contrary to the Constitution void.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts act as 'bulwarks' against legislative encroachments and protect private rights from transient public passions; independence thus mitigates unjust, partial, or iniquitous laws and deters legislatures from passing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judiciary as intermediate interpreter of Constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: The courts are designed to be an intermediate body between the people and the legislature, to keep the latter within limits assigned to their authority; interpretation of the laws and Constitution is the proper province of the courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the legislature's acts conflict with the Constitution, judges should prefer the Constitution (the people's will) to statutes; this does not imply judicial superiority but subordination of both to the people's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule on conflicting authorities (statutes and constitutional hierarchy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When two statutes conflict, the rule of construction is that the last in order of time is preferred; but where acts of superior and subordinate authorities conflict, the prior act of the superior prevails; the Constitution prevails over statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The last-in-time rule is a practical construction among coequal authorities; between superior and subordinate authorities, priority of the superior is the natural rule. Courts must use fair construction but adhere to hierarchy when irreconcilable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for strict rules, precedents, and specialized legal skill
rubrics_metrics.description: A voluminous code of laws necessitates strict rules and precedents that judges must study; few men will have the skill and integrity required for judgeships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because legal precedent will swell to great bulk and require long, laborious study, permanency in office is necessary to attract and retain the qualified characters needed to administer justice with utility and dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judiciary is the least dangerous department but requires protection
rubrics_metrics.description: From the nature of its functions, the judiciary has neither force nor will, having only judgment, and is therefore the weakest of the three departments; nonetheless, it requires care to enable it to defend itself against attacks from the other branches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This weakness justifies protections (tenure, compensation, impeachment rules) so courts can perform their role without being overborne by executive or legislative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper objects/scope of the federal judicature (enumerated classes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The federal judiciary ought to extend to: (1) cases arising out of the laws of the United States passed pursuant to constitutional powers; (2) cases concerning execution of the articles of Union; (3) cases in which the United States are a party; (4) cases involving the peace of the Confederacy (intercourse with foreign nations or among States); (5) cases originating on the high seas and of admiralty or maritime jurisdiction; and (6) cases in which State tribunals cannot be supposed impartial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These categories are justified by needs for uniform enforcement of constitutional restrictions, national responsibility to foreigners, prevention of inter-state conflict, and impartial adjudication where local bias is likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal jurisdiction for disputes affecting national peace, foreigners, and inter-state equality
rubrics_metrics.description: The national judiciary should have cognizance of causes involving foreigners, controversies between States, between a State and citizens of another State, between citizens of different States, citizens of the same State claiming lands under different States, and disputes between States/citizens and foreign states/citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral of such disputes to national tribunals ensures impartiality, preserves the public faith toward foreign powers, prevents partiality of local courts, and secures equal privileges and immunities across the Union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coextensiveness of judicial with legislative authority for uniformity
rubrics_metrics.description: The judicary authority of the Union ought to be coextensive with the legislative authority when necessary to give efficacy to constitutional provisions and to ensure uniform interpretation of national laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirteen independent final courts interpreting the same national laws would cause contradiction and confusion; a single national judicial power ensures uniformity and effective enforcement of constitutional restrictions on states.
